exchanges.analyst: None (scripted management discussion led by Dan Pooley)
exchanges.question: Not an analyst exchange: scripted results review and moderated management discussion (Q3 performance, guidance changes by segment, model year 2027 early order programs, dealer inventories, precision ag technology, closing thoughts) before analyst Q&A opened.
exchanges.answer: Q3 results and FY2026 outlook given (see metrics and guidance); Q3 included $110 million of incremental IEPA tariff refunds, FY2026 refunds $382 million, no further refunds assumed; direct tariff expense ~$1.1 billion for FY excluding refunds. C&F backlogs extend well into fiscal 2027, producing modestly below retail; PPA order books effectively full, South America industry revised to down 15%-20%, underproducing retail there. North American EOP orders for planters and sprayers up mid-single digits vs completion of last year's program; management views 2026 as the bottom of the ag equipment cycle with a measured, not sharp, recovery in 2027. Used MY2023-2024 high-horsepower tractor inventory down nearly 40% YoY; See & Spray factory adoption to nearly double (about 1/3 of NA sprayers on order); over 40% of MY2027 NA planters with advanced offerings.

exchanges.question: Setup for 2027: production vs retail by region; and with EOP up mid-single digits, what are 2027 pricing expectations given concerns about farm equipment cost inflation?
exchanges.answer: Seibert: modest underproduction this year in PPA and C&F, a couple percentage points for each; PPA driven by caution in South America, C&F by retail growth with orders four to five months out. Kovar: EOP pricing rolled out several months ago; focus remains on covering inflation with pricing across EOP products and the PPA portfolio for 2027. No specific price figure given.

exchanges.question: What drove the tariff expectation falling to $1.1 billion (tariff relief for ag equipment in July or refunds)? Follow-up: update on the excavator launch and timing of broader adoption.
exchanges.answer: Seibert: FY2026 run rate updated from $1.2 billion to $1.1 billion, excluding refunds, mainly from Section 232 changes (roughly 25% rate on imported goods dropped to 15%, given European imports); effective 1st June, so five of 12 months this year, implying a further tailwind in fiscal 2027. Norwood: first Deere-designed excavator models launched this spring, three models in market, shipments getting to customers, very positive feedback; more models roll out over the next three to four years; early days.

exchanges.question: Did shipments slip from 4Q into 3Q, and does the inventory-to-sales ratio suggest Deere built tractor inventory in 3Q ahead of the industry; how is the cadence exiting the year?
exchanges.answer: Seibert: don't read too much into Q3; shipment plans set for the year with orders on hand; pulled ahead some demand to manage Q4 risk; nothing to be concerned about on inventory. Kovar: sold-ahead positions and retail pace on trend with historical averages; North America tractor shipments started slowly and are catching up. Norwood: PPA and C&F Q4 net sales similar to Q3; no refund benefit in Q4; PPA and SAT margins lower in Q4 on seasonal high R&D and SA&G.

exchanges.question: How might mix, especially higher technology sales in C&F and precision ag EOP take rates, influence 2027, relative to the 2- to 3-point mix benefit discussed in stronger years?
exchanges.answer: Too early to tell; uncertainty from input and commodity volatility, shipment disruptions (Black Sea), recent softness in the E.U. and Brazil; construction fundamentals good and its growth could affect mix; EOP tech adoption and how the programs and combines wrap up will drive mix. Encouraged by signals but no figure given.

exchanges.question: What regional variability is there in the EOP, and could the mid-single-digit growth end in the high single-digit range as the programs wind down?
exchanges.responderTitle: President, Worldwide Agriculture & Turf Division, PPA, Sales and Marketing, Americas and Australia
exchanges.answer: A couple of weeks remain on sprayer EOP and a bit longer on planters; U.S. trending slightly better than Canada, which is a very limited part of the planter business; time will tell whether mid-single digit turns more positive. Best signals are technology take rates: doubling of See & Spray on factory-installed sprayer orders and 40% of planters taking the most advanced planting technologies.

exchanges.question: Has the cadence of EOP orders been driven by recent grain price improvement or by technology decisions; were orders already up a month and a half ago?
exchanges.responderTitle: President, Worldwide Agriculture & Turf Division, PPA, Sales and Marketing, Americas and Australia
exchanges.answer: Wouldn't read much into cadence, which has been as expected; EOP tweaked this year to give dealers more choice; pleasantly surprised by technology take rates; hopeful the mid-single digit increase holds.

exchanges.question: Are 8 Series tractor orders tracking the better EOP trend in North America? And will Europe, with heat and input cost stress, respond to a crop price recovery the way the U.S. would?
exchanges.answer: 8R orders as expected; orders four to five months out; model year 2026 shipment schedule basically closed, collecting Q1 orders; corn futures about $5.05 a good signal. Brazil runs a three-month order book; Q4 orders in hand, industry guide changed, too early to tell for 2027; the move financing program at single-digit rates may help. Europe mixed: arable farmers more challenged, Small Ag & Turf supported by stable dairy and livestock cash flows; overall order pace as expected, no recent step-up.

exchanges.question: How are C&F order programs shaping up, and how much is dealer rental fleet loading and what is the outlook for that theme?
exchanges.answer: C&F order trends very positive: about four to five months of orders on hand vs typical two to three months. Drivers: large infrastructure projects, data center starts, independent rental channel participation and dealer-owned rental fleet opportunity; 2026 underproduction gives a 2027 opportunity. No quantification of rental fleet loading.

exchanges.question: Given remaining Section 232 benefit in 2027 and no further refunds in Q4, is the roughly $800 million net 2026 tariff impact a headwind, tailwind or neutral for 2027, all else equal?
exchanges.answer: Net tariffs will be a headwind into next year: about $1.1 billion direct tariffs less $382 million refunds gives net exposure of approximately $750-ish this year; next year run rate expected closer to right around $1 billion, a step up in tariff expense versus this year.

exchanges.question: C&F pricing: why does guidance imply lower price in Q4 versus +8% in Q3? And how large could Deere's dealer rental business become and how does it change the economics?
exchanges.answer: Seibert: C&F price guide started the year at 2.5%, moved to 3%, rounded down to 2.5%, now back up (full-year 3 points); Q3 +8% partly an easy comp against about 5% negative price in Q3 2025 from incentives; Q4 orders in hand, nothing outsized, road building contributes. Norwood: opportunity to increase rental exposure via independent rental houses and dealers; 30%-35% of earthmoving transactions start as a rental and growing; dealer appetite to expand rental fleets could boost inventory fill next year; no size target or economics given.

exchanges.question: What merchandising incentives and EOP pricing trends imply for margins next year (up, down, neutral)? And what does the FTC right-to-repair settlement mean for the aftermarket business and the $2 billion-$3 billion lifecycle parts opportunity over five years?
exchanges.answer: Seibert: taking measured inflationary price, committed to cover inflation over time, nothing outsized; pricing set at several points in the year; inflation dynamic (oil prices, supplier tariffs). No margin direction given. Norwood: Deere has always supported customers' ability to repair their own equipment, unchanged; agreement formalizes existing tools such as John Deere Operations Center PRO Service (diagnostics, digital manuals, self or independent software updates); supports long-term lifecycle solutions aspirations. No comment on the $2 billion-$3 billion figure.

exchanges.question: Will the 2028 European CAP budget policy change pull demand forward into 2027 or cause farmers to delay; any directional 2027 forecast for Europe?
exchanges.answer: Too early to tell; order book four to five months out, just collecting Q1 orders; arable sentiment depends on input costs and commodity prices, dairy and livestock fairly stable. Too early to say whether policy pulls demand forward or delays it; no 2027 forecast.

exchanges.question: How are Brazilian and U.S. farmers positioning on input costs and how might that affect crop and equipment decisions?
exchanges.responderTitle: President, Worldwide Agriculture & Turf Division, PPA, Sales and Marketing, Americas and Australia
exchanges.answer: Uncertainty on input prices everywhere; fertilizer impact differs between Brazilian and U.S. farmers; farmers looking for alternatives in products, amounts and sources. Not seeing a huge reduction in intended application; still focused on yield; larger farmers have multiple years of inputs contracted and are reconsidering.
